card.programme: Wong ancestry-recombination graphs · deterministic sample extraction
card.title: Sample ancestry can be extracted exactly from the actual interval records

plain_language.question: Can we extract exactly the ancestry supported by the chosen samples without assuming an ideal parent oracle?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Yes. The actual interval-record scanner and memoized traversal return exactly the supported local edges. They recover every original local edge if and only if all those edges are sample-supported.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Reuse a proved actual-record extraction procedure and its abstract write/check/lookup bounds, with sample support and persistent identities explicit.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This is not an unconditional inverse of arbitrary unsampled graphs, an MRCA-truncating simplifier, a machine-time benchmark, a byte-format round trip or tskit conformance.

card.exact_statement_and_scope: For every finite acyclic interval GARG on a finite node type and linearly ordered coordinates, use decidable node equality and coordinate tests. Supply record and sample lists with exactly the memberships of its record and sample sets; repeated entries and arbitrary order are allowed. At each coordinate x where every child has at most one local parent, the executable actual-record scan followed by memoized rootward tracing with fuel N=card(Node) returns parent p at c exactly when the original edge p→c is active at x and c is a sample or an ancestor of a sample at x. The ancestor-count rank proves fuel adequacy and is not an input oracle. Persistent IDs and unary ancestors are retained. If unique local parents hold at all coordinates, equality of the complete extracted parent-array family with every original indexed local edge relation holds if and only if the source is SampleSupported: every active local edge has a child with a sample descendant, allowing equality. This is an edge-relation round trip, not equality of interval subdivisions, hidden event histories, dates, metadata or bytes. It is not local-MRCA truncation. Starting with an empty functional cache, the run has writes≤N and checks, lookups≤writes+sample-list length. These counters hold even for cyclic parent functions or inadequate fuel; exact extraction correctness has the separate acyclicity/fuel premises. Root and unvisited entries both use none, so roots may be looked up repeatedly. No constant-time scanner/cache/allocation or machine-time assumption is hidden in the inequalities.

origin.detail: The existing Samuel Wong programme formalizes the source's sample-rootward extraction and an actual interval-record/memoized implementation. This recovers a completed source-specific theorem, not a new claim of solving every source operation.

card.prior_work: Credit Wong et al. 2024 Appendix E sample-rootward traversal, standard memoization and ancestry restriction, and Lean/Mathlib. The existing Samuel package supplies actual-record correspondence, cache-completeness refinement, node-cardinality fuel and exact sample-support/counter contracts. Historical novelty is not adjudicated; this card is archival recovery.
card.our_contribution: The existing Samuel source connects the actual record scanner to the local graph, proves cache-completeness and equality with a reference traversal, obtains node-cardinality fuel without an algorithmic rank oracle, and states the exact sample-support round trip and abstract operation bounds. This card restores that completion rather than proving it again.
card.novelty_status: Historical novelty is not adjudicated. Known operations and classical suppliers retain credit; archival recovery does not create new proof authorship or priority.
card.remaining_obligation: None identified for the exact completed actual-record extractor, sample-support criterion and abstract counter bounds in the bounded source recovery.
card.separate_downstream_or_validation_work: Incremental across-coordinate tables; machine arrays/cache representation; record-scan, allocation and runtime bounds; fully executable whole-graph export; arbitrary-file parsing and byte/metadata round trips; external tskit conformance. These are distinct from the completed per-coordinate theorem.
